content.content:
# AGENTS.md

Project: Weekly_Research_Review

## What this is
"Research in 5": a weekly review of one research paper Eric picks, for Baylor
Athletics cross-functional health and wellness staff, the Applied Performance team,
and admin/leadership. Each week produces a 5-slide Baylor-branded deck in dark and light
themes (the dark PDF is posted in the MS Teams channel), a Teams post, and a plain-text
email for training staff outside Teams. Every review answers the same four questions: What did the researchers do? What
were the results? What does this mean? What are the coaching takeaways? It also rates how
much to trust the paper. A running index keeps past reviews searchable.

Eric supplies the paper: a PDF, a DOI or URL, or a Zotero item.

## How to run a review
Follow `docs/WORKFLOW.md` step by step. Content rules, length limits, and the
evidence-level rubric are in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. The one-command build is:

```
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive   # build + QA locally
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug            # then publish to Drive
```

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reviews/NNN_slug/review.json` | The review content. Source of truth for deck, post, and email. Committed. |
| `reviews/NNN_slug/notes.md` | Extraction notes with page numbers for every number used. Committed. |
| `reviews/INDEX.md` | Generated index of past reviews. Committed. |
| `templates/review.template.json` | Blank review to copy. |
| `tools/build.js` | Validates review.json, writes dark and light decks, teams.md, email.txt to `build/`. |
| `tools/index.js` | Rebuilds INDEX.md and the Drive index CSV. |
| `tools/publish.ps1` | build, PowerPoint export to PDF and PNGs, index, copy to Drive. |
| `build/` | Local outputs. Gitignored. |

Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\`
(`_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` from DEV). One folder per review holds the dark and
light pptx and pdf, teams.md, email.txt (with `_vN` suffixes for revisions), and the
paper PDF. `_Inbox/` is where Eric drops new papers.
`Research_in_5_Index.csv` at the top is the staff-facing index.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Paper PDFs never go in git (copyright). They live in the Drive review folder.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Never invent or compute a number. Every figure in a review traces to a page in the paper.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Weekly_Research_Review

## What this is
"Research in 5": a weekly review of one research paper Eric picks, for Baylor
Athletics cross-functional health and wellness staff, the Applied Performance team,
and admin/leadership. Each week produces a 5-slide Baylor-branded deck in dark and light
themes (the dark PDF is posted in the MS Teams channel), a Teams post, and a plain-text
email for training staff outside Teams. Every review answers the same four questions: What did the researchers do? What
were the results? What does this mean? What are the coaching takeaways? It also rates how
much to trust the paper. A running index keeps past reviews searchable.

Eric supplies the paper: a PDF, a DOI or URL, or a Zotero item.

## How to run a review
Follow `docs/WORKFLOW.md` step by step. Content rules, length limits, and the
evidence-level rubric are in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. The one-command build is:

```
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive   # build + QA locally
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug            # then publish to Drive
```

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reviews/NNN_slug/review.json` | The review content. Source of truth for deck, post, and email. Committed. |
| `reviews/NNN_slug/notes.md` | Extraction notes with page numbers for every number used. Committed. |
| `reviews/INDEX.md` | Generated index of past reviews. Committed. |
| `templates/review.template.json` | Blank review to copy. |
| `tools/build.js` | Validates review.json, writes dark and light decks, teams.md, email.txt to `build/`. |
| `tools/index.js` | Rebuilds INDEX.md and the Drive index CSV. |
| `tools/publish.ps1` | build, PowerPoint export to PDF and PNGs, index, copy to Drive. |
| `build/` | Local outputs. Gitignored. |

Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\`
(`_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` from DEV). One folder per review holds the dark and
light pptx and pdf, teams.md, email.txt (with `_vN` suffixes for revisions), and the
paper PDF. `_Inbox/` is where Eric drops new papers.
`Research_in_5_Index.csv` at the top is the staff-facing index.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Paper PDFs never go in git (copyright). They live in the Drive review folder.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Never invent or compute a number. Every figure in a review traces to a page in the paper.

# Sketchbook

![sample](sample.png)

Graphite and one accent colour on a warm sketchbook page. Every line is drawn by hand and boils on 2s. Things get **pencilled in, inked over, then coloured with a quick scribble**, and hand lettering on the page does the narrating. The page is the world: its dot grid, spiral binding, smudges and coffee ring stay in view, and the camera moves across the page instead of cutting away from it.

## Palette (`SK` in kit.js)

| role | value | use |
|---|---|---|
| paper | `#f2ead8` | the page; also the blank sheet a morph happens on |
| ink | `#2a2420` | settled lines, lettering, eyes |
| graphite | `#6f6a63` (light `#9a948b`) | construction lines, the mess, hatching, things not settled yet |
| **accent: terracotta** | `#d97757` (shade `#b85c3f`) | the hero, and only the hero |
| highlighter | `#f7d64a` | the one word to read; one glowing object (a bulb, the sun) |
| red marker | `#e0483a` | a title underline or a stamp, once per scene |
| green | `#4f9d5d` | a check mark (done / correct) |
| prop colours | pencil `#f1bf2c`, wood `#ecc995`, eraser `#ef9aa6`, tape `#efe2b4`, card `#fffdf6` | real objects on the desk keep their own colours, kept small |

## Line and texture

- **Two pens.** `gline` is ink: one confident stroke plus a thin second pass that doesn't quite agree. `gpencil` is graphite: two light, looser passes. Use graphite for anything provisional and ink once it's decided.
- **The boil.** The wobble's phases reseed on every boil step (`B`), and it's index-based, so the tremor travels along the stroke. Structure (where a scribble goes, how long a hatch line runs) is seeded by key and never moves. Only the tremor changes.
- **Colour sits off the line.** `gfill` lays a flat colour a few pixels off the ink, the way a quick colour pass misses the outline.
- **Shading is hatching,** never a gradient. `ghatch` goes inside a clip, and `litHatch` shades a round thing but leaves a lit circle top-left.
- **Colour is a scribble.** `scribbleFill` shades a shape in one colour with a back-and-forth stroke, over a faint wash. It can write on.
- **The page** (`sketchPage`) is built once from a seeded RNG and cached: tooth specks, fibres, a vignette, a dot grid (or `ruled`), graphite smudges, ghosts of erased lines, a coffee ring, the edges of the pages below, and a spiral binding along the top. `post()` adds faint grain that boils on top.
- **Overshoot.** `loopPts` circles run past their start and drift outward. `sketchBox` boxes end a little past the corner they began at.

## Lettering

- Local system fonts only. Hand: `"Ink Free", "Segoe Print", "Bradley Hand", "Comic Sans MS", "Chalkboard SE", cursive` (the head's `HAND`). Marker: `"Segoe Print", "Marker Felt", "Bradley Hand", "Comic Sans MS", cursive` (`SK_MARKER`).
- `handLetter` places each glyph separately with jitter that boils, and adds a pen-weight stroke so thin system hand fonts read at phone size. With `reveal` 0..1, letters write on one at a time: each fades in, rises a little and grows to full size.
- A highlighter swipe (`highlight`, multiplied under the ink) lands on **one** word per caption, after the line is down. A red `underline` marks a title.
- Captions are short (about 20 characters a line, two lines at most, 80px), centred on `CX`, sitting at y ≈ 1330–1420.

## Motion habits

- **On 2s** (`TT` steps every 2 frames). Everything boils, including the page grain.
- **Things are drawn, not popped.** An object is pencilled on (`part`), inked over, then scribbled in colour, and the pencil prop (`pencilTool` at `writeEnd(...)`) follows the line as it goes. Rubbing something out uses `eraserTool` and crumbs.
- **Quick cuts are steps of one move.** The source ran at 30fps / 112.5 BPM, so a beat is 16 frames, an 8th 8 and a 16th 4. Cuts and write-ons landed on that grid, and a run of 16th cuts was one gesture, not separate shots. At 24fps / 120 BPM a 16th is 3 frames.
- The hero acts with squash and stretch (`sx`, `sy`), a hop on the beat, eyes that look at the subject (`look`) and blink, and a mood (`calm`, `wow`, `happy`, `puzzled`). Small graphite marks show what it's feeling: `?`, `!`, `sweat`, `sparkle`.
- The camera leans in on the subject and pulls back to show the world, always across the same page.

## Frame checklist (sketchbook)

1. **Graphite carries everything.** Count the colours. Ink and graphite should do most of the drawing, terracotta appears only on the hero, and highlighter yellow appears only on the word to read or the one glowing thing. If a second thing turns terracotta, the colour no longer means "the hero".
2. **Lettering is the narrator.** The caption says the beat in under about 20 characters a line, with one highlighted word. You should be able to read it at phone size without the picture.
3. **The page is the world.** Some page should show in every frame: the grid, the binding, a smudge or the page edge. Nothing full-bleed covers it, and the morph happens on the bare page.
4. **Write-ons instead of pops.** New things are drawn on: pencil first, then ink, then colour. Only a reaction gets a pop: a `!`, a stamp, a hop.
5. **Mess is graphite; what's settled is ink.** Raw input, clutter and first tries are pencil tangles (`graphiteScribble`). Results are inked, neat and few.
6. **Everything boils, nothing swims.** Structure stays fixed while the tremor changes on 2s. Nothing should slide smoothly on 1s, apart from the camera.
7. **One subject, one gesture.** At any moment one thing is being drawn, and the pencil is on it. Background life (a plane looping the margin, an ant on a line, twinkling margin stars, chimney smoke, birds) is graphite and small.
8. **Safe area.** Content stays inside x 60–940, y 250–1500. The tag sits at y ≈ 340 and the caption at y ≈ 1330–1420.

## Kit API (`styles/sketchbook/kit.js`)

- **Lines:** `gline(P, { w, col, a, key, amp, part, step, second, closed })`, `gpencil(P, { w, col, a, key, amp, part, passes, closed })`, `gwob(P, key, amp)`, `writeOn(P, part)`, `writeEnd(P, part)` (where the pen is), `closeP(P)`
- **Shapes:** `loopPts(cx, cy, rx, ry, over, a0, n)`, `sketchBox(x, y, w, h, r, over)`; core's `ellipsePts`, `arcPts`, `xform` and `bbox` still work
- **Colour and shade:** `gfill(P, col, { a, off, key })`, `gclip(P)`, `ghatch(x0, y0, x1, y1, { ang, gap, col, w, a, key })`, `litHatch(P, {...})`, `scribbleFill(P, col, { ang, gap, w, part, base, key })`, `graphiteScribble(cx, cy, w, h, key)`, `smudge(x, y, rx, ry, a, rot)`
- **Lettering:** `handLetter(str, x, y, size, { face: 'hand' | 'marker', col, align, reveal, key, jit, rot, stroke })` returns `[x0, x1]`, `letterW(str, size, face)`, `highlight(x0, x1, y, h, part)`, `underline(x0, x1, y, { col, part })`
- **Page:** `sketchPage({ grid: 'dots' | 'ruled' | 'plain', tint, tintA })`, `pageTex(grid)`
- **Props:** `pencilTool(tx, ty, ang, s)`, `eraserTool`, `paperPlane`, `noteCard(x, y, rot, s, lines, key)`, `inkStamp(str, x, y, s, rot, a)`, `checkMark(x, y, s, part)`, `sparkle(x, y, r, k)`, `arrowPencil(P, part)`, `sweat(x, y, k)`, `scrap(x, y, rot, s)`, `tapeStrip(x, y, w, rot)`, `doodleStar(x, y, r)`, `doodleBird(x, y, s, flap)`
- **Hero:** `doodleHero(x, y, r, { mood, look, sx, sy, rot, legs, step, arms, key })` sets `SPARK_AT`
- **Captions (DEFER):** `pageTag('sketch it')`, `pageCaption(['line one', 'line two'], [[1, 'word']], { y, size, at })`
- **STYLE:** `backdrop` (the page washed toward a colour), `window` (the world through a graphite outline lifted by a soft smudge shadow), `blob` (a colour scribble inside a graphite outline), `hero`, `heroColor` (terracotta), `heroPts`, `post` (boiling grain)
- **Needs from the head:** `HAND`, `CX`

## Do / don't

- **Do** draw things on in order (pencil, ink, colour), have the pencil prop follow the line, and keep props small and real.
- **Do** key every random value: `key` for structure, with `B` mixed in for the tremor. The page cache is static and seeded.
- **Do** give a house or tree crown a paper `gfill` before its ink, so graphite behind it doesn't show through.
- **Don't** use a second accent colour, gradients for shading, flat drop shadows (use a smudge), or type that looks typeset.
- **Don't** reuse core names (`ink`, `pencil`, `hatch`, `resample`, `trace`, `ellipsePts`, `rrectPts`). The kit's versions are `gline`, `gpencil`, `ghatch`, `loopPts`, `sketchBox`.
- **Don't** load web fonts, images or URLs (`build.mjs` rejects them). Fonts are the local stacks above.
- **Don't** fill the frame edge to edge with drawing. Leave paper.

**Proven on:** a 15s explainer (a hand-lettered short with no voice-over, 30fps / 112.5 BPM); this demo (6s, 24fps / 120 BPM, a lightbulb doodle morphs into the sun over a sketched hill).

# Craft: the rules that came out of building these pieces

Each rule was learned the hard way on a real piece. Follow them unless the user asks otherwise; if one turns out wrong, propose a change.

## Story
- **The plot is a true process.** The real steps, in their real order; every beat follows from the one before. Pace belongs to what a beat *means*, not to fixed seconds.
- **One constant the eye can hold** — a hero, a stage, a page — while everything else changes.
- **Colour means one thing** for the whole piece (e.g. orange = the machine's mind, red = sound). Never spend that colour on decoration.
- **Silence before the payoff, loudest on the payoff.** A 0.5–4s drop to near-silence on a held image, then the single loudest hit. Find the beat the true story already has (video models were silent until 2025; ChatGPT appeared on an empty box).
- **The busiest moment is not the loudest.** Peak density goes just before the silence; the loud hit is the turn.
- **The end is the start, changed.** Return to the opening image with the difference that the story made (Turing's page, now answered).
- **One device you can say in a sentence** ("the spark gains a ray each era").
- **A history's facts can supply the arc** — and must be true. Web-check every date and number; say "a", not "the first", unless sourced.

<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Research in 5 #001</title>
<style>
  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; background: #1d1a17; overflow: hidden; }
  body { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
  canvas { height: min(100vh, calc(100vw * 16 / 9)); width: auto; aspect-ratio: 9 / 16; display: block; cursor: pointer; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<canvas id="c" width="1080" height="1920"></canvas>
<script>
"use strict";
// =====================================================================
//  RESEARCH IN 5 #001 — 9:16, 24.0s @ 120 BPM, 24fps, sketchbook.
//  Saraee et al. 2026: in 22 elite volleyball players with jumper's knee in one knee, 0 of 7 alignment
//  angles differed between the sore knee and the pain-free one. The hero blames its leg shape, the check
//  says "same", and the piece ends on the review's bottom line: load and landing first, leg shape second.
//  Every number on screen is from reviews/001_alignment-jumpers-knee/review.json (page-cited).
// =====================================================================
const FPS = 24, W = 1080, H = 1920;
const BPM = 120, BEAT = 60 / BPM, E8 = BEAT / 2, E16 = BEAT / 4;
const DURATION = 24.0;
const NFRAMES = Math.round(DURATION * FPS);
const LOOP_T = NFRAMES / FPS;
const SAFE = { top: 240, bottom: 420, right: 140 };
const HAND = '"Ink Free", "Segoe Print", "Bradley Hand", "Comic Sans MS", "Chalkboard SE", cursive';
const CX = 500;

const ERA_LIST = [[0, 5, () => sceneHunch()], [5, 14, () => sceneCheck()], [14, 24, () => sceneSoWhat()]];
const SHOTS = [
  ['hunch', 0, 0.0, 5.0, 'one knee hurts; the hero pictures a bent leg and wonders if its build is to blame'],
  ['check', 1, 5.0, 14.0, 'both legs measured: 7 angles tick "about the same"; silence; the SAME stamp'],
  ['sowhat', 2, 14.0, 24.0, 'the hero jumps while a tally grows; back to the opening, pain gone: load and landing first'],
];
const TIMELINE = {
  width: W, height: H, fps: FPS, bpm: BPM, duration: DURATION, frames: NFRAMES, loop: LOOP_T, safe: SAFE,
  format: 'morph-chain',
  shots: SHOTS.map(([key, era, t0, t1, title], i) => ({ id: i + 1, key, era, t0, t1, title })),
  cuts: [],
  morphs: [5.0, 14.0],
  cues: {
    bubble: 0.75, legs: 1.0, q: 2.25, lean: 3.75,
    legsDraw: 5.5, ticks0: 7.0, tick: 0.5, cap2: 10.75, hush: 12.0, stamp: 13.0,
    jump0: 15.0, jumps: 8, home: 19.5, cap4: 19.75, src: 20.75,
  },
  acts: [

# Brief: RI5 #001 social clip (pilot, run 1)

## Spec
- 1080x1920 (9:16), 24fps, 120 BPM, 24.0s = 576 frames. Music only, composed in code.
- Style: sketchbook (graphite, terracotta hero, one highlighted word per caption).
- Format: morph chain, 3 eras, 2 shape morphs (5.0s sore-knee ring to X-ray knee ring; 14.0s hero to hero).
- Device: the hero blames its leg shape; the check says SAME; the thought bubble that held a bent leg ends up holding a jump tally.

## Beats
| t (s) | what happens | sound |
|---|---|---|
| 0-5 | one knee hurts; the hero pictures knock-kneed legs, "?" | thin pad, pencil scratches |
| 5-10.75 | two legs (sore, pain-free); 7 angles tick "about the same" | a rising pluck per tick |
| 10.75-12 | "0 of 7 different. biggest gap < 1°" | the busiest bar |
| 12-13 | hold, hero puzzled | silence |
| 13-14 | SAME stamp over the legs | the loudest hit, flat chord |
| 14-19.5 | the hero jumps; a tally mark per landing | soft plucks on landings |
| 19.5-24 | back to the opening image: no pain, the tally in the bubble; source line | faint bed, decays |

## Claims and sources
Every number comes from `reviews/001_alignment-jumpers-knee/review.json`, which was verified against the paper
(Saraee et al. 2026, J Orthop Surg Res, doi 10.1186/s13018-026-07229-w). This replaces the skill's web-check rule:
the paper is a better source than a web search.
- 22 elite male volleyball players: p. 3.
- 7 alignment angles from standing X-rays, 5 at the knee and 2 at the ankle: Table 3, p. 6.
- 0 of 7 different (all p >= 0.107) and the largest mean gap under 1 degree (0.84 for aLDTA): Table 3, p. 6.
- "load + landing first, leg shape second" is the review's own bottom line (`takeaways.bottom_line`), marked on screen
  as one 22-player study. The paper did not measure jump load; it names it as the likely factor (p. 7).

# Social animations (pilot)

Short animated clips for social media, one per review, made with the `animate` Claude Code skill
(github.com/cth9191/animate, MIT). Pilot status: one clip built (#001, 2026-10-07). Not part of the weekly
workflow until Eric decides it earns a place.

## Setup (per machine)
- Node 18+, ffmpeg on PATH (both already on the Baylor laptop).
- `npm i -g playwright && npx playwright install chromium`
- `git clone https://github.com/cth9191/animate vendor/animate && git -C vendor/animate checkout 7e5eb56`
  (`vendor/` is gitignored. Pinned to 7e5eb56, v0.4.0, because the upstream repo is days old and changes fast.)
- Not installed as a global skill on purpose: project-level until it proves itself.

## Make a clip
Pieces live in `animations/NNN_slug/` (piece.json, src/, brief.md, LOG.md committed; builds and renders ignored).
```
T=vendor/animate/plugins/animate/skills/animate/tools
node $T/build.mjs animations/NNN_slug          # one index.html; open it in a browser to preview
node $T/storyboard.mjs animations/NNN_slug     # key frames for approval
node $T/export.mjs animations/NNN_slug --share # renders/share.mp4 (add --formats 9:16,1:1,16:9 for more shapes)
node $T/review.mjs animations/NNN_slug         # measured checks: story arc, text, loudness, dead beats
```
Copy `renders/share.mp4` to the review's Drive folder as `RI5-NNN_slug_social_vN.mp4`.

## Rules
- Every number on screen comes from the review's `review.json` (already verified against the paper), and the
  clip shows the source line. No number appears that the deck does not carry.
- One finding per clip, honest about the study's size and design. A cute character must not overclaim.
- Who posts it, and on which account, is not decided. Baylor Athletics brand approval may apply.

## Pilot cost (#001)
- Wall time: about 3 minutes per export on this laptop; rendering costs no tokens.
- Tokens: about 90k of context across the whole pilot. About 35k was one-time reading (the skill's docs, the
  sketchbook kit and demo). The piece itself is about 300 lines of code (scenes 170, head 60, score 25, bridges 15).
  A second clip reuses the reading and starts from #001's files, so expect well under half.

entries.name: SendUserFile
entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

content.text:
The pilot clip is built: a 24-second vertical sketchbook animation of Research in 5 #001 (Saraee 2026, jumper's knee). I've sent you the video and its storyboard, and it's on Drive too.

**Your token question:** it's moderate, not a ton. JavaScript itself costs nothing in tokens, and rendering and checking run on your laptop for free. The whole pilot used about 90k tokens:
- **About 35k was one-time reading** of the skill's docs and the sketchbook drawing code.
- **The clip itself is about 300 lines of code**, which is the real per-clip cost.
- **A second clip should cost well under half.** It skips the reading and starts from #001's files.

Each export takes about 3 minutes of laptop time.

**What the clip does (24s, music only):**
- A little character with one sore knee wonders if its leg is "built wrong".
- Both legs get measured, and 7 angles tick "about the same": *0 of 7 different, biggest gap < 1°*.
- A beat of silence, then a red **SAME** stamp.
- The character jumps while a tally of jumps grows, and it ends on the review's bottom line: *load + landing first, leg shape second.*
- Every number comes from #001's already-verified review, and a source line says it's one study of 22 players.

**Checks:** the tool's automated review passes everything: the payoff is the loudest moment, no text overlaps, and phone loudness is −14.7 LUFS. The first run failed two checks: the stamp covered the checklist and the ending was too loud. I fixed both and re-ran it. Captions are readable at phone size.

**Caveats:**
- **Nobody has listened to it yet.** I can't hear audio, so watch it with sound before posting.
- **I skipped your three approval steps** (story, look, storyboard) to get the pilot done. Normally you'd sign off on each.
- **Weakest shot:** the legs in "the check" are thin sticks.
- **Who posts it**, and whether Baylor Athletics brand approval applies, are still open.

**Install:** the tool isn't installed as a global skill. It's a pinned copy inside the Research in 5 project, so none of your skill or harness setup changed. Playwright is now installed globally on this laptop.

**Where things are:**
- Video: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\001_alignment-jumpers-knee\RI5-001_alignment-jumpers-knee_social_v1.mp4`
- Code: branch `worktree-animate-pilot` in Weekly_Research_Review, pushed, commit `1caae8b`, not merged. To open a PR: https://github.com/erash11/Weekly_Research_Review/pull/new/worktree-animate-pilot
- How-to, rules and cost: `docs/ANIMATION.md`

**Next:** watch it, then decide whether clips become an optional weekly output. If you like it, I can run `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` on the animate skill using what this run showed. The main fix it would surface: let the approval steps go faster when the facts come from an already-verified review.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Weekly_Research_Review

## What this is
"Research in 5": a weekly review of one research paper Eric picks, for Baylor
Athletics cross-functional health and wellness staff, the Applied Performance team,
and admin/leadership. Each week produces a 5-slide Baylor-branded deck in dark and light
themes (the dark PDF is posted in the MS Teams channel), a Teams post, and a plain-text
email for training staff outside Teams. Every review answers the same four questions: What did the researchers do? What
were the results? What does this mean? What are the coaching takeaways? It also rates how
much to trust the paper. A running index keeps past reviews searchable.

Eric supplies the paper: a PDF, a DOI or URL, or a Zotero item.

## How to run a review
Follow `docs/WORKFLOW.md` step by step. Content rules, length limits, and the
evidence-level rubric are in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. The one-command build is:

```
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive   # build + QA locally
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug            # then publish to Drive
```

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reviews/NNN_slug/review.json` | The review content. Source of truth for deck, post, and email. Committed. |
| `reviews/NNN_slug/notes.md` | Extraction notes with page numbers for every number used. Committed. |
| `reviews/INDEX.md` | Generated index of past reviews. Committed. |
| `templates/review.template.json` | Blank review to copy. |
| `tools/build.js` | Validates review.json, writes dark and light decks, teams.md, email.txt to `build/`. |
| `tools/index.js` | Rebuilds INDEX.md and the Drive index CSV. |
| `tools/publish.ps1` | build, PowerPoint export to PDF and PNGs, index, copy to Drive. |
| `build/` | Local outputs. Gitignored. |

Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\`
(`_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` from DEV). One folder per review holds the dark and
light pptx and pdf, teams.md, email.txt (with `_vN` suffixes for revisions), and the
paper PDF. `_Inbox/` is where Eric drops new papers.
`Research_in_5_Index.csv` at the top is the staff-facing index.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Paper PDFs never go in git (copyright). They live in the Drive review folder.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Never invent or compute a number. Every figure in a review traces to a page in the paper.

# Memory Index

One line per memory: title, file, and a hook that says when to open it.
Never put memory content here — the file itself holds the facts.

- [Printing Press spec traps](project_printing-press-spec-traps.md) — writing a CLI spec
- [zsh shell traps](project_zsh-shell-traps.md) — a zsh script misbehaves
- [Status report sourcing](project_status-report-sourcing.md) — building the status report

# AGENTS.md

Project: Weekly_Research_Review

## What this is
"Research in 5": a weekly review of one research paper Eric picks, for Baylor
Athletics cross-functional health and wellness staff, the Applied Performance team,
and admin/leadership. Each week produces a 5-slide Baylor-branded deck in dark and light
themes (the dark PDF is posted in the MS Teams channel), a Teams post, and a plain-text
email for training staff outside Teams. Every review answers the same four questions: What did the researchers do? What
were the results? What does this mean? What are the coaching takeaways? It also rates how
much to trust the paper. A running index keeps past reviews searchable.

Eric supplies the paper: a PDF, a DOI or URL, or a Zotero item.

## How to run a review
Follow `docs/WORKFLOW.md` step by step. Content rules, length limits, and the
evidence-level rubric are in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. The one-command build is:

```
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive   # build + QA locally
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug            # then publish to Drive
```

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reviews/NNN_slug/review.json` | The review content. Source of truth for deck, post, and email. Committed. |
| `reviews/NNN_slug/notes.md` | Extraction notes with page numbers for every number used. Committed. |
| `reviews/INDEX.md` | Generated index of past reviews. Committed. |
| `templates/review.template.json` | Blank review to copy. |
| `tools/build.js` | Validates review.json, writes dark and light decks, teams.md, email.txt to `build/`. |
| `tools/index.js` | Rebuilds INDEX.md and the Drive index CSV. |
| `tools/publish.ps1` | build, PowerPoint export to PDF and PNGs, index, copy to Drive. |
| `build/` | Local outputs. Gitignored. |

Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\`
(`_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` from DEV). One folder per review holds the dark and
light pptx and pdf, teams.md, email.txt (with `_vN` suffixes for revisions), and the
paper PDF. `_Inbox/` is where Eric drops new papers.
`Research_in_5_Index.csv` at the top is the staff-facing index.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree and branch on disk; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: Required true when action is "remove" and the worktree has uncommitted files or unmerged commits. The tool will refuse and list them otherwise.

# Handoff 2026-10-07: animate pilot (social clip for #001)

## What and why
Eric asked whether github.com/cth9191/animate (a Claude Code skill that makes short procedural canvas animations
rendered to MP4) could make cute social clips for Research in 5 and 5 Slides in 5 Minutes. Verdict: worth a pilot,
not a pipeline yet. He said run the pilot. One 24s 9:16 sketchbook clip of #001 was built and passes every check.

## Decisions
- Vendored, not installed as a skill: a gitignored clone at `vendor/animate`, pinned to 7e5eb56 (v0.4.0, the repo
  was three days old). Reason: the skill-promotion rule (project-level until it proves itself) and the Friday harness
  budget. Nothing in `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.agents` changed. Playwright was installed globally (`npm i -g`).
- Paper: #001, because it was actually sent to staff on 2026-10-06; #002 has not gone out.
- Numbers on screen come only from review.json (already verified against the paper), not from web searches.
- The skill's three approval steps (story, look, storyboard) were skipped for the pilot. A real run asks Eric.
- The SAME stamp sits over the legs, not the checklist: the review caught it covering the labels.
- Work stays on branch `worktree-animate-pilot` (draft PR), not main.

## Files
- `animations/001_alignment-jumpers-knee/` piece.json, src/head.html, src/scenes.js, src/bridges.js, src/score.js,
  brief.md, LOG.md (generated index.html, frames/, renders/, review/, storyboard.png are gitignored)
- `docs/ANIMATION.md` (setup, commands, rules, measured cost), `docs/STATUS.md`, `.gitignore`
- Drive: `07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5/001_alignment-jumpers-knee/RI5-001_alignment-jumpers-knee_social_v1.mp4`

## Measured
- Review: story arc 5/5, text 0 overlaps, loudest at 13.0s in the payoff, 0.8s silence before it, -14.7 LUFS.
- Export 2m50s. Tokens about 90k for the whole pilot, about 35k of it one-time reading; the piece is about 300 lines.

## Next
1. Eric watches the clip with sound.
2. Decide who posts and whether brand approval applies (STATUS open question).
3. If it earns a place: run `mattpocock-skills:writing-for-agents` on the skill, and try a 1:1 and 16:9 export
   (`--formats 9:16,1:1,16:9`). Thicker bones in shot 2 is the known weak spot.

# AGENTS.md

Project: Weekly_Research_Review

## What this is
"Research in 5": a weekly review of one research paper Eric picks, for Baylor
Athletics cross-functional health and wellness staff, the Applied Performance team,
and admin/leadership. Each week produces a 5-slide Baylor-branded deck in dark and light
themes (the dark PDF is posted in the MS Teams channel), a Teams post, and a plain-text
email for training staff outside Teams. Every review answers the same four questions: What did the researchers do? What
were the results? What does this mean? What are the coaching takeaways? It also rates how
much to trust the paper. A running index keeps past reviews searchable.

Eric supplies the paper: a PDF, a DOI or URL, or a Zotero item.

## How to run a review
Follow `docs/WORKFLOW.md` step by step. Content rules, length limits, and the
evidence-level rubric are in `docs/CONTENT_SPEC.md`. The one-command build is:

```
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug -NoDrive   # build + QA locally
pwsh tools/publish.ps1 reviews/NNN_slug            # then publish to Drive
```

## Layout
| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reviews/NNN_slug/review.json` | The review content. Source of truth for deck, post, and email. Committed. |
| `reviews/NNN_slug/notes.md` | Extraction notes with page numbers for every number used. Committed. |
| `reviews/INDEX.md` | Generated index of past reviews. Committed. |
| `templates/review.template.json` | Blank review to copy. |
| `tools/build.js` | Validates review.json, writes dark and light decks, teams.md, email.txt to `build/`. |
| `tools/index.js` | Rebuilds INDEX.md and the Drive index CSV. |
| `tools/publish.ps1` | build, PowerPoint export to PDF and PNGs, index, copy to Drive. |
| `build/` | Local outputs. Gitignored. |

Drive: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\07_EDUCATION\Research_in_5\`
(`_DRIVE/07_EDUCATION/Research_in_5` from DEV). One folder per review holds the dark and
light pptx and pdf, teams.md, email.txt (with `_vN` suffixes for revisions), and the
paper PDF. `_Inbox/` is where Eric drops new papers.
`Research_in_5_Index.csv` at the top is the staff-facing index.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Paper PDFs never go in git (copyright). They live in the Drive review folder.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Never invent or compute a number. Every figure in a review traces to a page in the paper.

# Brief: RI5 #001 social clip (pilot, run 1)

## Spec
- 1080x1920 (9:16), 24fps, 120 BPM, 24.0s = 576 frames. Music only, composed in code.
- Style: sketchbook (graphite, terracotta hero, one highlighted word per caption).
- Format: morph chain, 3 eras, 2 shape morphs (5.0s sore-knee ring to X-ray knee ring; 14.0s hero to hero).
- Device: the hero blames its leg shape; the check says SAME; the thought bubble that held a bent leg ends up holding a jump tally.

## Beats
| t (s) | what happens | sound |
|---|---|---|
| 0-5 | one knee hurts; the hero pictures knock-kneed legs, "?" | thin pad, pencil scratches |
| 5-10.75 | two legs (sore, pain-free); 7 angles tick "about the same" | a rising pluck per tick |
| 10.75-12 | "0 of 7 different. biggest gap < 1°" | the busiest bar |
| 12-13 | hold, hero puzzled | silence |
| 13-14 | SAME stamp over the legs | the loudest hit, flat chord |
| 14-19.5 | the hero jumps; a tally mark per landing | soft plucks on landings |
| 19.5-24 | back to the opening image: no pain, the tally in the bubble; source line | faint bed, decays |

## Claims and sources
Every number comes from `reviews/001_alignment-jumpers-knee/review.json`, which was verified against the paper
(Saraee et al. 2026, J Orthop Surg Res, doi 10.1186/s13018-026-07229-w). This replaces the skill's web-check rule:
the paper is a better source than a web search.
- 22 elite male volleyball players: p. 3.
- 7 alignment angles from standing X-rays, 5 at the knee and 2 at the ankle: Table 3, p. 6.
- 0 of 7 different (all p >= 0.107) and the largest mean gap under 1 degree (0.84 for aLDTA): Table 3, p. 6.
- "load + landing first, leg shape second" is the review's own bottom line (`takeaways.bottom_line`), marked on screen
  as one 22-player study. The paper did not measure jump load; it names it as the likely factor (p. 7).
